leakage_rule: features of a pitch row use only turns strictly before the pitch's cut, the first decision of any kind by any investor (so the cut does not depend on the outcome); never decides or negotiates turns, never turns of a negotiation exchange
label: pitch-held-out estimate
penalty_rule: per outer training fold and model: leave-one-pitch-out up to 25 training pitches, else 5 grouped folds; log loss with equal weight per pitch; ties to the larger penalty

not_fitted.note: not fitted by any ladder model (descriptive columns of features.csv): every `_n` count behind a mean or share, the H5 frame-match share (a_frame_match_share), the exposure columns beyond the spec's C1 list (demo_seconds, prepared_seconds) and the count of answers with a reaction window (rx_answers), a denominator of the reaction shares

both_passes.note: both annotation passes averaged for every numeric feature (spec 6.4 a)

rates.note: exposure as rates per minute, not counts (spec 6.4 b)

non_development.note: without the pilot development videos named by the selection file (`--selection`, else the run's own; spec 6.4 c); every video was looked at while the instrument was shaped (plan v4 section 11), so this removes the pilot videos, not the looking

fixed_penalty_10.note: ridge penalty fixed at 10 in every fold, not chosen inside it (spec 6.4 d)

all_stage_a.note: C2 adds the rank score of every Stage A item, not the primary one only (spec decision 9)

h9_populations.support: all answers (rated on checkable support and admitted uncertainty)
h9_populations.full: answers rated on support, uncertainty, substance, coherence and context

h9_exchange_sensitivity.note: outcomes read on the model's exchange grouping, unstable between passes: computed as a sensitivity, not reported, no direction stated

single_feature_note: each numeric feature on its own: correlation with the outcome (interval: bootstrap over pitches), leave-one-pitch-out log-loss gain of a one-feature ridge logistic head (penalty 1) over the training base rate, the head's standardised coefficient on all rows, and the partial correlation given the number of questions asked. Features observed on less than 30% of the rows, or constant, are left out. Descriptive ranking, not a test

significance.bootstrap_p: two-sided bootstrap p-value from the same pitch-resampling draws as the interval: 2 x the smaller of the share of draws at or below the null value and the share at or above it, never below 1 / (draws + 1)

permutation.note: permutation test of 'this model predicts held-out pitches no better than the offer rate'. Null: no association between a pitch's pre-decision features and its sharks' outcomes, keeping the dependence of the outcomes within a pitch. In each permutation every pitch's whole set of known outcomes is handed to another pitch with the same number of sharks with a known outcome (on pitch rows that is a plain shuffle of the pitch outcomes), in random order within the pitch, since sharks of different pitches do not correspond; the feature rows stay where they are. The full leave-one-pitch-out fit is then repeated (preprocessing fitted on the training pitches of each fold), with the ridge penalty of each model fixed at the value its inner cross-validation chose most often in the real run, so the penalty search is not repeated; the observed statistic is computed in the same way (log_loss, auc), and the real run's inner-CV log loss is given beside it (log_loss_inner_cv). p = (1 + number of permutations at least as good as observed) / (1 + n_perm), for log loss (lower is better) and for AUC (higher is better), pitches weighted equally

fdr.note: p_value: two-sided pitch-level permutation p-value of the correlation (each pitch's set of outcomes is handed to another pitch with the same number of rows; p = (1 + permutations with a correlation at least as large in size) / (1 + permutations)); p_boot: the bootstrap p-value from the interval's draws; q_value: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment of p_value within this table; significant_fdr: q < 0.05

significance.coefficients: standardised coefficients (log-odds per 1 SD of a numeric feature, per level of a category) of the full exploratory model refitted on all rows with a known outcome, the ridge penalty fixed at the value the leave-one-pitch-out run chose most often. Intervals and p-values resample whole pitches and refit the model with the preprocessing held fixed. These are conditional associations inside one penalised model: each depends on which other features are in it, the penalty shrinks all of them towards zero, and correlated features share their weight. Not independent effects

ranking_agreement.scope: computed over all ranked videos of the run, not only the analysed ones: a video's standing is relative to the other clips of its batch

books.note: codebook spellings and the Stage A item list come from each video's own bundle folder (bundle) when it holds the instrument, otherwise from the live release (live)

shark_level.note: the archived shark-level design (analysis.archive.shark_level.run), for the F1 paragraph; reported, not tested
